run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-18T00:25:30Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend is explained by total failure of the frontend's ad call path. From the 00:25:30 bucket to 00:33:30 the frontend's ERROR span rate rose from 0 to 8.04/s (4.422/s at 00:29:30, matching the alert's stated value), and its GET /api/data, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans all switched to ERROR with no successful /api/data spans in those buckets, alongside new dns.lookup and tcp.connect ERROR spans. The ad service emitted no spans of any operation during those buckets, and its replacement pod — created by an ad Deployment rollout at 00:24:27 (new ReplicaSet ad-5f8dd7c58d, ad-554b849958 scaled to 0) — first logged 'Ad service starting.' at 00:29:09, 'Ad service started, listening on 8080' at 00:30:49 and its first request at 00:32:43, so it was not serving for roughly 8 minutes after the rollout, which is exactly when the frontend failed. A simultaneous payment rollout (payment-5d565cf9b, 00:24:26) coincided with a single 2-minute burst of checkout PaymentService/Charge and PlaceOrder ERORES. Both Deployments were restarted with byte-identical pod templates (same image, same env), and ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config currently holds two enabled fault-injection flags naming exactly these services: adFailure 'Fail ad service' = on and paymentUnreachable 'Payment service is unavailable' = on. On that pattern that ConfigMap is reported as the candidate root cause, but the investigation is partial: the declared fault effect (ad returning errors) was not observed — ad emitted zero error spans and served requests normally once listening — the flagd logs are empty, and there is no change history, so when those flags changed and what triggered the 00:24 rollouts remain unknown. The frontend is the only entity with sustained, self-evidenced impact; frontend-proxy also emitted its own error spans in the same window and checkout briefly did.

claims.text: The frontend ERROR span rate (traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}) was 0 at every returned point up to 00:23:30, then 0.478/s at 00:25:30, 8.044/s at 00:27:30, 4.4222/s at 00:29:30, 4.644/s at 00:31:30, 3.867/s at 00:33:30 and 0 at 00:35:30 (the last sample; the data ends 00:35:30). The 4.4222/s reading at 00:29:30 matches the value quoted in the alert.

The frontend's failing span operations in the 31 minutes ending 00:35:18 were GET /api/data (407.57), executing api route (pages) /api/data (407.57), grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (407.57), POST /api/checkout (79.28), executing api route (pages) /api/checkout (79.28), grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (79.28) and tcp.connect (15.25), all with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR.

Per-operation frontend rates show the /api/data path failing completely: GET /api/data ERROR 1.189/s at 00:27:30, 1.100/s at 00:29:30, 1.156/s at 00:31:30, 0.967/s at 00:33:30 and 0 at 00:35:30, while GET /api/data STATUS_CODE_UNSET was 0 at 00:27:30, 00:29:30 and 00:31:30 (0.222/s at 00:33:30, 1.256/s at 00:35:30). grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds ERROR mirrored those values exactly, and dns.lookup (0.011–0.044/s) and tcp.connect ERROR (0.033–0.089/s) spans appear only inside this window.

The ad service emitted no spans at all during the failure: oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, getAdsByCategory and getRandomAds were all 0/s at the 00:25:30, 00:27:30, 00:29:30, 00:31:30 and 00:33:30 buckets, recovering to 1.244/s GetAds and 0.978/s getAdsByCategory at 00:35:30; ad's own ERROR span rate was ~0 throughout (0.011/s only at 00:21:30 and 00:35:30).

Error-span rate by service over the same 2-minute points: frontend peaked at 8.044/s; frontend-proxy was 0.333/s at 00:25:30, 3.889/s at 00:27:30, 2.256/s, 2.378/s, 2.022/s and 0.033/s at 00:35:30; checkout had 1.516/s only at 00:27:30; ad and recommendation showed 0.011/s at isolated points; accounting, fraud-detection and payment were 0 at all 16 returned points.

In the checkout service, oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge both showed STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0.7578/s in the single 00:27:30 bucket and 0 at every later bucket, while PlaceOrder STATUS_CODE_UNSET continued at 0.933/s (00:29:30), 0.922/s (00:31:30) and 0.789/s (00:33:30, 00:35:30).

Events in otel-demo show a rollout of both workloads: Deployment ad scaled up new ReplicaSet ad-5f8dd7c58d from 0 to 1 at 00:24:27 and scaled ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0 at 00:24:29, pod ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 was Scheduled 00:24:27 and Created/Started 00:24:29, and ad-554b849958-6z62j was 'Killing - Stopping container ad' at 00:24:29; Deployment payment scaled up payment-5d565cf9b 0→1 at 00:24:26 with pod payment-5d565cf9b-8gwcn Started 00:24:30 and scaled payment-55766d76b9 1→0 at 00:24:30. All these events are Normal, and no Warning pod events (Unhealthy, BackOff, Evicted, Failed) appear for either workload.

The ad Deployment's two ReplicaSets have identical pod templates — ad-554b849958 (revision 1, replicas 0) and ad-5f8dd7c58d (revision 2, replicas 1) both use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad with the same env (AD_PORT=8080, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://$(OTEL_COLLECTOR_NAME):4318) — and the payment pair is likewise identical (both payment-55766d76b9 and payment-5d565cf9b use ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment with PAYMENT_PORT=8080, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013).

The replacement ad container's retained stdout starts late and ramps slowly: the earliest line read is 'Ad service starting.' at 2026-11-18T00:29:09.972878021Z, followed by 'Ad service started, listening on 8080' at 00:30:49.975023314Z, and its earliest request line 'Targeted ad request received for [travel]' appears only at 00:32:43.073961138Z.

Once serving, the ad pod handled requests with no error lines ('no baggage found in context' plus 'Targeted/Non-targeted ad request received' lines from 00:32:43 to 00:34:14), and the payment pod logged paired 'Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.' lines at 00:28:41–00:28:59 and 00:31:08–00:31:28.

Current pod state: ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 and payment-5d565cf9b-8gwcn are Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-18T00:24:27Z / 00:24:26Z; the frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-68tcg has been Running/Ready since 2026-11-17T23:51:39Z with restartCount 0, and no otel-demo pod shows more than 1 restart (fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-n79gv = 1).

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config holds fault-injection flags whose names name exactly the restarted services, with the fault switched on: adFailure defaultVariant "on" (description "Fail ad service", state ENABLED) and paymentUnreachable defaultVariant "on" (description "Payment service is unavailable", state ENABLED); the other flags read (adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) all have defaultVariant "off".

Naming the setting holder as the candidate root cause: ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config carries adFailure=on and paymentUnreachable=on, whose names refer to the ad and payment services that were restarted with unchanged pod templates at 00:24:26–00:24:30 while the frontend's own failures are on the GetAds and PaymentService/Charge call paths, and no other object in the evidence applies a change or fault to those workloads.

Service wiring is intact now: Service ad selects opentelemetry.io/name=ad on port 8080 and its endpoints point at the new pod ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 (100.96.1.149); Service payment selects opentelemetry.io/name=payment on port 8080 and its endpoint is payment-5d565cf9b-8gwcn (100.96.1.157).

Pre-incident baseline from Jaeger: the newest ad-related traces the backend holds are from 00:08:50–00:09:03 and contain no error rows (10 ad oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans with rpc.grpc.status_code="0", 10 frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans with rpc.grpc.status_code="0", frontend GET /api/data spans with http.status_code 200).

Mechanism of the alert: the ad Deployment rollout at 00:24:27 replaced the serving pod with one that served no request until about 00:32:43, so frontend GetAds calls failed (client ERROR spans with no matching ad server spans, new dns.lookup/tcp.connect spans, no ad request log lines before 00:32:43), which made GET /api/data fail entirely and drove the frontend RequestErrorRate alert. The ad-side unavailability, not an ad application error, is what the span and log evidence shows.

The short checkout/payment error burst (PaymentService/Charge and PlaceOrder ERROR 0.758/s in the 00:25:30–00:27:30 bucket only) is more consistent with the simultaneous payment rollout at 00:24:26 than with a sustained payment outage, because the payment container logged successful charges from 00:28:41 onward and the checkout-side Charge errors stopped after that bucket.

The two enabled flags in flagd-config (adFailure, paymentUnreachable) are the trigger for the 00:24:26–00:24:30 rollouts of the ad and payment Deployments and therefore for the failures; this is unproven because the flagd container produced no readable log lines and no change history is available, so neither the time of the flag change nor the rollout trigger could be observed.

The declared 'Fail ad service' effect was not observed at the ad service itself: ad had zero ERROR spans (its error series is ~0, only 0.011/s at 00:21:30 and 00:35:30) and no error log lines, and every request it logged after starting was handled normally, so the frontend failures came from ad not being reachable rather than from ad returning application errors.

A sustained 'Payment service is unavailable' state was not observed either: the payment pod logged successful charge/transaction pairs at 00:28:41–00:28:59 and 00:31:08–00:31:28 and payment's own error-span rate was 0 at all 16 returned 2-minute points, with only one 2-minute burst of Charge errors seen from the checkout side.

The ad and payment pods are Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and their events in otel-demo are all Normal rollout events (ScalingReplicaSet, SuccessfulCreate, SuccessfulDelete, Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started, Killing) with no Unhealthy, BackOff, Evicted, OOMKilled or Failed events, so crash, OOM or probe-driven eviction is not what removed ad from service.

Rejected: that the ad pod crashed, was OOMKilled or was evicted and thereby stopped serving. Its restartCount is 0, it is Running/Ready, and no crash, OOM or eviction event exists for it; the container start at 00:24:29 is followed by a first retained log line only at 00:29:09, so the gap is a slow/unavailable service, not a crash loop.

Check audit/change history (the change_history integration is not available in this Run) for who edited ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config and for the rollout of Deployments ad and payment at 00:24:26–00:24:30, to establish whether the adFailure/paymentUnreachable flags were switched on in that change.

If these faults are not intended, set the flagd-config variants adFailure and paymentUnreachable back to "off"; if they are intended, treat the ad/payment rollouts they accompany as the known disruption mechanism and avoid restarting those single-replica Deployments during load.

Investigate the ad container's startup latency (first retained log line 00:29:09 after container start 00:24:29, then about 100 seconds to 'listening on 8080', and the first request at 00:32:43) by checking its CPU limits/throttling and its flagd client initialisation, since a single-replica rollout of this workload removes ad from service for the whole startup period.

gaps: No change history / audit source is integrated in this Run, so when adFailure and paymentUnreachable in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config were switched on, by whom, and what triggered the 00:24:26–00:24:30 restarts of Deployments ad and payment are unknown.

The declared fault itself was not observed happening: ad produced zero error spans and served requests normally once listening, so it could not be confirmed that the adFailure flag produced ad-side errors rather than the observed connection-level unreachability.
The flagd container (flagd-78f7f46ddc-f756g: init-config, flagd, flagd-ui) returned no log lines for 00:18–00:36, so flag reload/change events could not be read.
A query for the ad pod's log lines in 00:24:20–00:29:00 returned no data, so whether the container logged anything before 00:29:09 is unknown rather than absent.
Jaeger holds no traces for the incident: its newest spans are from 00:09:03, so no span-level error status or error text exists for the failing 00:25–00:33 requests.
The frontend pod's stdout returned 0 bytes for 00:23–00:36, so the frontend's own error text for the failing /api/data requests could not be read.

No kube-state-metrics series are exposed by this Prometheus (queries for kube_* returned no data), so ad/payment pod readiness between 00:24:29 and 00:32:43 cannot be confirmed; a query for NetworkPolicy objects returned no objects, so whether one existed during the window is unknown.
The root cause of the slow ad container startup is unexplained; CPU throttling, node pressure and image/flagd initialisation were not observable with the available sources.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be read from Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules with rule_name RequestErrorRate returned no data), so the alert expression and its evaluation window are unverified.
All metric samples end at 00:35:30, roughly 9 minutes before the query time, so the state between 00:35:30 and 00:44:18 is unknown.
next_steps: Confirm with the platform owners or the GitOps/audit trail whether the 00:24 change set included edits to flagd-config (adFailure, paymentUnreachable) and rollouts of the ad and payment Deployments.
Inspect the ad container's resource limits and CPU throttling, and capture a deliberate restart of a single ad replica, to reproduce and measure the non-serving window.
Review whether the frontend /api/data route should hard-fail when the ad dependency is unavailable, since all /api/data spans in the failing buckets were errors.
If the flags are not meant to be active, revert adFailure and paymentUnreachable to off and verify with flagd that the variants are off.
Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule definition from the alerting configuration to confirm which series and threshold produce the warning.
